newsitem.title: UK: Man Utd beat AC Milan with merchandising.
newsitem.headline: Man Utd beat AC Milan with merchandising.

text.p: Strong sales of club merchandise helped give English soccer champions Manchester United Plc higher turnover than Italian soccer rivals AC Milan in 1995/96, a report on Wednesday said.
Manchester United led the way in Europe the season before last, accountants Deloitte & Touche said in its annual review of football finance.
United had annual turnover, excluding transfer fees, of 53.3 million stg in 1995/96, ahead of Bayern Munich (46.6 million), Milan (45.4), Juventus (42.5) and Barcelona (41.3), the report said.
Comparing United and Milan in detail, the study noted the English club scored with annual merchandising income of 18.7 million stg against just 3.9 million for Milan.
It said Milan's sales were limited by the fact it does not own its own stadium, which reduces the opportunity for retail outlets. Pirated merchandise is also more common in Italy.
United has developed its brand to the point that it is exploring the potential for merchandise sales in the Far East.

United also had a much smaller wage bill than Milan, the study said. Milan's wage bill of 31.4 million stg represented almost 70 percent of income whereas United paid out 13.3 million -- a quarter of its annual revenue.

United was floated in 1991 and now have a market value of around 420 million stg. Milan, owned by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, is one of a number of Italian clubs considering a stock market listing.
